correctness.rationale: A four-one word is determined by its five zero-run lengths. Any Abelian-square factor contains 0, 2 or 4 ones; zero-only squares give floor(max(r_i)/2); two-one factors are unique triples (gap,u,v) obeying equal-half parity and |u-v|<=gap with occurrence bounds (union prevents duplicate substrings); four-one factors are unique (u,v) under exact half-boundary inequalities. An independently coded direct-substring vs run-count comparison checked all four-one words through length 22. Separately compiled and ran the assigned combinatorial C++ counting implementation afresh through n=128; it exhaustively processed 275234400 four-one configurations and output minimum and multiplicity table for every n=4..128, matching floor((n+2)/4) and 2,2,8,4 for all 110 target lengths. Separately checked every proposed optimizer word and reversal at each of the 110 lengths against the exact run formula, verified the full proposed family has the exhaustively certified minimizer count, and therefore ruled out additional minimizers within the finite range. It does not extrapolate to n>=129; independent direct substring checking covers a shorter range than the optimized enumeration.
